raw_response:
Well, it's that time of year again. I've got 4.5 mu to work with, just me and my wife — the kids are working in Shijiazhuang now. Thirty years I've been at this, since I was 18. I switched from grain to vegetables about 12 years ago when I saw that cabbage and eggplant could bring in more cash per mu, but it's more work and more risk too. With only 4.5 mu and two mouths depending on it, every yuan I spend on inputs has to come back to me, or we're in trouble.

I'm keeping my **cabbage-eggplant** system as the backbone. I've got **1.5 mu of spring cabbage** going in now. I bought hybrid seedlings from the market — about 70 yuan per mu — because saved seed gives me uneven heads and the buyer from the wholesale market docks me for that. I'll put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before transplanting, then topdress with 8 kg of urea per mu when the heads start forming. Last year I tried cutting back on the base fertilizer to save money, and the heads were too loose — I lost more than I saved. For irrigation, I've got my well, but electricity for the pump isn't free. I'll irrigate three times: right after transplanting, at rosette stage, and when heading starts. Cabbage worms were bad two years ago, so I'll spray insecticide twice and fungicide once. Me and my wife can handle most of it, but for transplanting I'll hire one day's help — 100 yuan.

**Eggplant** takes another **1.5 mu**, and that's my summer income. I buy seedlings for this too — about 130 yuan per mu — because eggplant seeds are finicky and I don't have a good place to start them early. I'll transplant in early May, once the soil warms up. Eggplant is a heavy feeder, so I'm putting 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the hole at planting, then side-dressing twice more: once at first flowering and again at peak fruiting, using compound plus a bit of extra urea. All told, that's about 20 kg N per mu, but split so it doesn't wash away. I'll need to irrigate at least 6 times if June is dry like last year. The pump will cost me, but wilting eggplant means no fruit set. For pests, it's the usual — aphids and wilt — so insecticide and fungicide both. This crop needs the most labor: staking, pruning, picking every few days for months. I'll hire two days of help for transplanting, but the rest is us.

I've got **half a mu of cauliflower** — similar to cabbage, planted a bit later in early April. Same fertilizer approach but a bit less: 15 kg N per mu total. **Another half mu of chili peppers** — I saved seeds from my best plants last year, so that saves me seed money. I'll transplant in mid-May. Chili doesn't need as much nitrogen, maybe 12 kg per mu, but it likes potassium for the fruit. **Kidney beans** on 0.3 mu — I saved the seed, and since they're legumes I don't need much nitrogen, just one application of compound at sowing. Good for my wife to sell fresh at the village gate. And a small patch of **spinach**, 0.2 mu, sown in early March. Quick money, harvest by May. One dose of fertilizer, a couple of irrigations, no pesticide needed.

For pesticides, I buy what the ag supply shop recommends — usually imidacloprid for insects and some generic fungicide. I don't like spraying more than I have to, but if I don't, the vegetables look bad and the middleman pays less.

Total costs? I'm figuring about **2,200 yuan** for the season. That's seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, electricity for the pump, and three days of hired labor at 100 yuan each. It's a big chunk of what I've got saved, but if cabbage sells at 1 yuan per jin and eggplant at 1.2, I should be okay. I'm not trying anything new this year — I can't afford to gamble. I'll do what worked before, watch what old Wang does across the road, and hope the weather cooperates.
